title: This lint warns about boolean comparisons in assert-like macros.
summary: It is shorter to use the equivalent. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for expressions of the form x == true, x != true and order comparisons such as x < true (or vice versa) and suggest using the variable directly.
summary: Unnecessary code. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Instead of using an if statement to convert a bool to an int, this lint suggests using a from() function or an as coercion.
summary: Coercion or from() is another way to convert bool to a number. Both methods are guaranteed to return 1 for true, and 0 for false. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the usage of &expr as *const T or &mut expr as *mut T, and suggest using &raw const or &raw mut instead.
summary: This would improve readability and avoid creating a reference that points to an uninitialized value or unaligned place. Read the &raw explanation in the Reference for more information. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for &*(&T).
summary: Dereferencing and then borrowing a reference value has no effect in most cases. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for a borrow of a named constant with interior mutability.
summary: Named constants are copied at every use site which means any change to their value will be lost after the newly created value is dropped. e.g. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of &Box<T> anywhere in the code.
summary: Check the Box documentation for more information. A &Box<T> parameter requires the function caller to box T first before passing it to a function. Using &T defines a concrete type for the parameter and generalizes the function, this would also auto-deref to &T at the function call site if passed a &Box<T>. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of Box<T> where T is a collection such as Vec anywhere in the code.
summary: Check the Box documentation for more information. Collections already keeps their contents in a separate area on the heap. So if you Box them, you just add another level of indirection without any benefit whatsoever. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: checks for Box::new(Default::default()), which can be written as Box::default().
summary: Box::default() is equivalent and more concise. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of Box<T> where an unboxed T would work fine.
summary: This is an unnecessary allocation, and bad for performance. It is only necessary to allocate if you wish to move the box into something. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.
